mechanism_narrative: The four-week monotonic rise in RETAIL_REC from -9.1 to -3.4 is a positive momentum signal; consumers are re-engaging with retail and recreation venues, so the next 28-day mean exceeds the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rises every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the four-week rise.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility recovering above the -30% threshold signals that mobility restrictions or remote-work policies are easing enough to support discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed RETAIL_REC over the last 14 days when TRANSIT is above -30.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising GROCERY_PHARM from 2.3 to 5.7 and falling RESIDENTIAL from 4.0 to 3.1 shows households shifting from home-centered to out-of-home routines; this substitution increases RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls, the next 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS below -15.0 indicates weather or seasonal conditions pushing outdoor recreation indoors; displaced park visits shift spending toward retail-and-recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: After PARKS falls below -15.0, the next 7-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than or equal to the prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues improving while WORKPLACES remains stable rather than deteriorating, commuter and errand traffic jointly support store visits; the interaction predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week and WORKPLACES does not fall below -7.5
failure_condition: When TRANSIT rises and WORKPLACES stays above -7.5, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden PARKS decline of more than 5 points week-on-week, while TRANSIT remains below -25, signals renewed caution or tightening restrictions that suppresses discretionary retail trips, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT is below -25
failure_condition: When PARKS falls >5 points week-on-week and TRANSIT < -25, the next 7-day RETAIL_REC mean is higher than or equal to the prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remaining above baseline but declining each week from 4.0 to 3.1 indicates a steady return to out-of-home activity; as people spend less time at home, retail-and-recreation mobility rises over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: The next 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 14-day mean when RESIDENTIAL declines week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM staying above baseline and rising to 5.7 indicates normalized essential shopping trips that spill over into adjacent retail-and-recreation errands, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite GROCERY_PHARM above baseline and rising, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the last 28-day mean.
